You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our
community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body
size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity
and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming,
diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our
community include:

* Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
* Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
* Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
* Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes,
  and learning from the experience
* Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the
  overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

* The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or
  advances of any kind
* Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
* Public or private harassment
* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email
  address, without their explicit permission
* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
  professional setting

## Enforcement Responsibilities

Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of
acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in
response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive,
or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject
comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are
not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation
decisions when appropriate.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when
an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces.
Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address,
posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed
representative at an online or offline event.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be
reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at
gh.dr3w@proton.me.
All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the
reporter of any incident.

## Enforcement Guidelines

Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining
the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

### 1. Correction

**Community Impact**: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed
unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

**Consequence**: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing
clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the
behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

### 2. Warning

**Community Impact**: A violation through a single incident or series
of actions.

**Consequence**: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No
interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with
those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This
includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels
like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or
permanent ban.

### 3. Temporary Ban

**Community Impact**: A serious violation of community standards, including
sustained inappropriate behavior.

**Consequence**: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public
communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or
private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction
with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period.
Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

### 4. Permanent Ban

**Community Impact**: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community
standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior,  harassment of an
individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

**Consequence**: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within
the community.

version 2.0, available at
https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct.html.

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by [Mozilla's code of conduct
enforcement ladder](https://github.com/mozilla/diversity).

- Output results to CSV:

import subprocess as sp
def run(args, inp="", env_home="/tmp/emptyhome"):
    e=dict(os.environ); e["HOME"]=env_home
    p=sp.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode

# -o tests: does -o write to file and also stdout? Earlier test showed stdout only has Failed line, file has content. So -o suppresses stdout content, writes to file.

    (["-S","-e","-o",tmp], "hello test@example.com\n"),
    (["-S","-e","-C","-o",tmp], "hello test@example.com\n"),
    (["-S","-e","-C","-l","-o",tmp], "hello test@example.com\n"),
]:
    try: os.remove(tmp)
    except: pass
    out,err,rc=run(args, inp)
    print(f"ARGS={args} OUT={out!r} RC={rc} FILE={open(tmp).read()!r}" if os.path.exists(tmp) else f"ARGS={args} OUT={out!r} NO FILE")

# -o with invalid path?

print(f"dir+o: OUT={out!r} FILE={open(tmp).read()!r}" if os.path.exists(tmp) else f"dir+o: OUT={out!r}")

]:

tmp="/tmp/pluglocal2"
import shutil
if os.path.exists(tmp): shutil.rmtree(tmp)

# start with one plugin
plugins=[{"arg_long_name":"myplug","help_message":"my help","content_type":"mytype","source_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8765/foo","version":"1.0","regex":"foo"}]
open(os.path.join(tmp,".DataSurgeon","plugins.json"),"w").write(json.dumps(plugins))
print("initial",open(os.path.join(tmp,".DataSurgeon","plugins.json")).read())
# update with new version? Need to serve new content for same URL
# Our server serves /tmp/plugcontent.json for any /main/plugins.json, currently contains last test's content. Let's set it to updated version
open("/tmp/plugcontent.json","w").write(json.dumps([{"arg_long_name":"myplug","help_message":"my help updated","content_type":"mytype","source_url":"ignored","version":"2.0","regex":"bar"}]))

# remove

print(f"remove OUT={out!r} ERR={err!r} RC={rc}")
print("after remove",open(os.path.join(tmp,".DataSurgeon","plugins.json")).read() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmp,".DataSurgeon","plugins.json")) else "no file")
# list after remove
out,err,rc=run(["--list"], stdin="", env=env)
print(f"list OUT={out!r} RC={rc}")

import subprocess, os, json, shutil, time
import subprocess as sp
def run(args, env_home, stdin=""):
    e=dict(os.environ); e["HOME"]=env_home
    p=sp.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode

def test_case(desc, home_setup, args):
    # home_setup: None (no dir), "no_file" (dir but no file), "empty" ([]), "invalid" ([{}]), "valid" ([one valid])
    tmp="/tmp/plugmatrix"
    if os.path.exists(tmp): shutil.rmtree(tmp)
    os.makedirs(tmp, exist_ok=True)
    ds=os.path.join(tmp,".DataSurgeon")
    if home_setup is None:
        # no dir at all
        pass
    elif home_setup=="no_file":
        os.makedirs(ds, exist_ok=True)
    elif home_setup=="empty":
        os.makedirs(ds, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(ds,"plugins.json"),"w").write("[]")
    elif home_setup=="invalid":
        os.makedirs(ds, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(ds,"plugins.json"),"w").write("[{}]")
    elif home_setup=="valid":
        os.makedirs(ds, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(ds,"plugins.json"),"w").write(json.dumps([{"arg_long_name":"test","help_message":"h","content_type":"c","source_url":"http://example.com","version":"1","regex":"r"}]))
    out,err,rc=run(args, tmp, stdin="y\n" if "[{}]" in str(home_setup) else "")
    print(f"{desc} setup={home_setup} args={args} RC={rc}\n OUT={out!r}\n ERR={err!r}\n---")

# Use timeout for invalid to avoid infinite loop? Use "y\n" to exit quickly for invalid parse? Actually invalid with --list and stdin y gives quick exit (1). For other commands, invalid parse also prompts? Let's test.
for setup in [None, "no_file", "empty", "valid"]:
    for args in [["--list"],["--add","http://127.0.0.1:8765/foo"],["--update","all"],["--update","http://example.com"],["--remove","http://example.com"]]:
        test_case("matrix", setup, args)
PY

# DataSurgeon

DataSurgeon (ds) is a versatile tool for extracting sensitive data and patterns from text and files. It can identify emails, phone numbers, hashes, credit cards, URLs, IP addresses, MAC addresses, DNS records, and more.

Key features:

- Cross-platform usage (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Recursive directory analysis
- Plugin support (runtime plugin usage may be available)
- CSV output for easy processing

Usage examples:

- Extract files listed on a webpage and deduplicate results:

  $ wget -qO - https://www.example.com | ds -F --clean | uniq

- Search a directory recursively and display filename and line number:

  $ ds --directory test_dir/ -Dl

- Output results to CSV:

// Load plugins for startup (before clap). Returns (plugins, had_open_error)
// If open fails, prints Failed once and returns empty.
// If parse fails (serde error due to missing fields or invalid type?), enters prompt loop (which never returns, exits or loops).

Let's test: what if plugins.json contains invalid JSON like "not json"? That would be parse error, should prompt? Let's check what original does for "not json" with --list and stdin y.
// For our earlier test with "not json" via --add remote, that was remote parse error (different message). For local file "not json", what happens? Need to test.
fn load_plugins_startup(path: &str) -> Vec<Plugin> {
    let content = match fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => {
            print_failed(path);
            return Vec::new();
        }
    };
    // Try to parse as Vec<Plugin>
    match serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Plugin>>(&content) {
        Ok(v) => {
            // Also need to validate regex? No, regex errors handled later? Probably not here.
            v
        }
        Err(e) => {
            // Check what kind of error: if it's due to missing fields or invalid type, prompt.
            // What about empty file? Or invalid JSON? Let's see: for "not json", serde error is "expected ident..." - would original prompt or print different?
            // We haven't tested local file with "not json". Let's assume all serde errors go to prompt.
            // But what about file containing "[]"? That's valid, no prompt.
            // For now, all errors go to prompt.
            let _ = e;
            prompt_loop_on_parse_error();
        }
    }
}

fn load_plugins_for_command(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Plugin>, String> {
    // For plugin commands that need to re-load and print second Failed if open fails.
    // Returns Ok(vec) or Err(open_failed) where open_failed means need to print Failed?
    // Actually caller will print Failed if open fails.
    match fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(c) => {
            match serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Plugin>>(&content) {
                Ok(v) => Ok(v),
                Err(_) => {
                    // For plugin commands with invalid file, what happens? It would prompt as well (same as startup).
                    // But startup already prompted? If startup prompted, we'd never reach here (since prompt loops/exits).
                    // So if we reach here, startup must have succeeded (file valid) or had open error (but then we wouldn't have valid?).
                    // Actually for plugin commands with invalid file, startup would have prompted already before parsing args, so we'd never get to command handling.
                    // Therefore this parse error case shouldn't happen here (since startup already handled).
                    // But to be safe, prompt again.
                    prompt_loop_on_parse_error();
                }
            }
        }
        Err(_) => Err("open_failed".to_string()),
    }
}

fn build_command(plugins: &[Plugin]) -> Command {
    let mut cmd = Command::new("DataSurgeon: https://github.com/Drew-Alleman/DataSurgeon")
        .version("1.2.8")
        .about("Note: All extraction features (e.g: -i) work on a specified file (-f) or an output stream.")
        .disable_help_flag(false)
        .disable_version_flag(false);
    // Add args in order as in help
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("file").short('f').long("file").value_name("file").default_value("").help("File to extract information from"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("add").long("add").value_name("add").default_value("").help("Adds a plugin from a GitHub repository (e.g ds --add https://github.com/Drew-Alleman/ds-winreg-plugin/)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("update").long("update").value_name("update").default_value("").help("Updates a plugin from a GitHub repository. You can also use `ds --update all` to update all plugins. (e.g ds --update https://github.com/DataSurgeon-ds/ds-cve-plugin/)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("remove").long("remove").value_name("remove").default_value("").help("Removes a plugin from a GitHub repository (e.g ds --remove https://github.com/Drew-Alleman/ds-winreg-plugin/)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("list").long("list").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("List all added plugins"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("clean").short('C').long("clean").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Only displays the matched result, rather than the entire line"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("directory").long("directory").value_name("directory").default_value("").help("Process all files found in the specified directory"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("ignore").long("ignore").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Silences error messages"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("line").short('l').long("line").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Displays the line number where the match occurred"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("thorough").short('T').long("thorough").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Doesn't stop at first match (useful for -C if multiple unique matches are on the same line"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("display").short('D').long("display").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Displays the filename assoicated with the content found (https://github.com/Drew-Alleman/DataSurgeon#reading-all-files-in-a-directory)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("suppress").short('S').long("suppress").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Suppress the 'Reading standard input' message when not providing a file"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("drop").long("drop").value_name("drop").default_value("").help("Specify a regular expression to exclude certain patterns from the search. (e.g --drop \"^.{1,10}$\" will hide all matches not under 10 characters)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("filter").long("filter").value_name("filter").default_value("").help("Include only lines that match the specified regex. (e.g: '--filter ^error' will only include lines that start with the word 'error'"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("hide").short('X').long("hide").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Hides the identifier string infront of the desired content (e.g: 'hash: ', 'url: ', 'email: ' will not be displayed."));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("output").short('o').long("output").value_name("output").default_value("").help("Output's the results of the procedure to a local file (recommended for large files)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("time").short('t').long("time").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Time how long the operation took"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("email").short('e').long("email").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract email addresses"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("phone").short('p').long("phone").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extracts phone numbers"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("hash").short('H').long("hash").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract hashes (NTLM, LM, bcrypt, Oracle, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, MD4)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("ip-addr").short('i').long("ip-addr").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract IP addresses"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("ipv6-addr").short('6').long("ipv6-addr").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract IPv6 addresses"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("mac-addr").short('m').long("mac-addr").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract MAC addresses"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("credit-card").short('c').long("credit-card").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract credit card numbers"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("url").short('u').long("url").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract urls"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("files").short('F').long("files").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract filenames"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("bitcoin").short('b').long("bitcoin").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract bitcoin wallets"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("aws").short('a').long("aws").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract AWS keys"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("google").short('g').long("google").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract Google service account private key ids (used for google automations services)"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("dns").short('d').long("dns").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract Domain Name System records"));
    cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new("social").short('s').long("social").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Extract social security numbers"));
    // plugins
    for p in plugins {
        cmd = cmd.arg(Arg::new(p.arg_long_name.clone()).long(p.arg_long_name.clone()).action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help(p.help_message.clone()));
    }

def ro(args, inp="", home="/tmp/emptyhome"):

    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode
def check(args, inp, home="/tmp/emptyhome"):
    n1,e1,r1=rn(args, inp, home)
    n2,e2,r2=ro(args, inp, home)
    ok=(n1==n2 and e1==e2 and r1==r2)
    print(f"{'MATCH' if ok else 'DIFF'} {args} {inp!r}")
    if not ok:
        print(f" NEW {n1!r} {e1!r} {r1}")
        print(f" OLD {n2!r} {e2!r} {r2}")
    return ok

# more
